html: The Malacatos were an Indigenous people of the warm valleys south of Loja in southern Ecuador, where the town of Malacatos still bears their name. They were neighbours of the Paltas and are often counted as part of that group. The Inca conquered the region in the late 1400s, and the Spanish founded the city of Loja nearby in the 1540s. Their language and customs were lost early in the colonial period, and little is known of them beyond Spanish records. See also the nearby Chaparra.
